newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MILOSEVIC RETURNS TO VILLA AFTER PERUGIA DEAL COLLAPSES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MILOSEVIC RETURNS TO VILLA AFTER PERUGIA DEAL COLLAPSES.

text.p: Aston Villa's Yugoslav striker Savo Milosevic pulled out of a proposed 4.5 million pounds ($7.5 million) move to Italian Serie A cub Perugia on Tuesday -- severely denting manager Brian Little's hopes of signing Liverpool's Stan Collymore.

Little had dropped the broadest hint on Tuesday that selling Milosevic held the key to being able to finance a 7.0 million pounds ($11.7 million) bid for Collymore who is out of favour at Liverpool, but now Milosevic has said he wants to remain at Villa Park.

It is unclear why Milosevic, signed by Little for 3.5 million pounds ($5.9 million) from Partizan Blegrade 16 months ago, has done a U-turn after apparently agreeing personal terms with the Italian club.
But Little said: "Savo is a little bit angry with Perugia because he feels he has been messed around a bit.
"I am a little bit surprised about what has happened but it is the decision of the player if he chooses not to sign for another club.
"I've had a good chat with Savo and made it clear that I as a manager want him to get his head down and get things right."
Milosevic, who reported back for training with Villa on Monday, stressed: "The Perugia thing is finished, definitely. Even if both clubs make the deal, I won't sign for Perugia.
"After all that has happened here, I want to help to give back something to Brian."
Milosevic will now be back in contention for a recall for Saturday's match at Coventry but being unable to now move for Collymore will be a blow for Little.
He had been looking to the former Nottingham Forest man to put back on course a season which has failed to ignite, with Villa making an early UEFA Cup exit and not making a title challenge.
Milosevic has failed to make a real impact at Villa scoring only 16 goals in 57 games for the club.
